title: One selected at random
hook: A fixed number of selections can be shared differently.

knows: Animals can act and respond to conditions.
doesNotKnow: In a toy model one member is chosen uniformly from a group. Is an individual’s chance smaller in a group of 3 or a group of 6?

misconception: One observed behavior always supports a broad or causal conclusion.
objective: In a toy model one member is chosen uniformly from a group. Is an individual’s chance smaller in a group of 3 or a group of 6?

claims.text: In a toy model one member is chosen uniformly from a group. Is an individual’s chance smaller in a group of 3 or a group of 6? With one uniformly selected individual, each member has chance 1/3 in the first group and 1/6 in the second. This is dilution under explicit assumptions, not a general prediction about real predator behavior or group safety.
claims.source: Stipulated toy observations; not observed animal data. Source lead, not checked: OpenStax Biology 2e, Behavioral Biology, https://openstax.org/books/biology-2e/pages/45-7-behavioral-biology

claims.text: The panels show a stipulated illustrative scenario, not observations or measurements of real animals.
One member is chosen uniformly from a group of 10. What is each member’s chance? One uniformly chosen member among ten gives each member probability 1/10.
